records.name: IDV1
records.title: A/C feed ratio change with B composition constant
records.base_description: A step disturbance changes the A/C feed ratio in stream 4 while the B composition remains constant. The fault affects reactant balance, reactor feed composition, reaction rate, recycle composition, and downstream separator and stripper behavior.
records.semantic_text: A step disturbance originating from an upstream feed control valve or metering pump malfunction alters the A/C feed ratio in stream 4 while maintaining B composition constant. This fault directly impacts the reactor, downstream separator, and stripper, disrupting reactant balance, feed composition, and reaction kinetics. Propagated variables include reactor temperature, pressure, and product purity, with control loops for feed ratio, separator level, and stripper reflux experiencing deviations. This semantic prototype is useful for zero-shot diagnosis because it explicitly links a specific disturbance source to cascading effects on unit operations and control variables, enabling fault identification through pattern recognition of causal relationships without prior fault data.

records.name: IDV2

records.base_description: A step disturbance changes the B composition in stream 4 while the A/C ratio remains constant. The inert component changes gas-phase dilution, reactor pressure, purge flow, recycle stream composition, and product separation behavior.
records.semantic_text: A step disturbance in the feed composition of component B to stream 4, while maintaining the A/C ratio, acts as the disturbance source. This affects the reactor, purge system, recycle stream, and product separation units by altering gas-phase dilution, reactor pressure, and recycle composition. Propagated variables include reactor pressure, purge flow rate, and recycle stream B concentration, impacting control loops for pressure regulation, purge flow, and composition control. This semantic prototype is useful for zero-shot diagnosis because it explicitly links the inert component’s role in dilution and phase behavior to cascading effects on multiple variables and units, enabling inference of fault mechanisms without prior training on specific fault instances.
